notes: Measured on the owner's 4x H200 NVL machine (GPUs 0-3; another workload ran on the machine's other four GPUs throughout, untouched). Power limit 450 W, clocks default, nothing changed for the measurement. Image ghcr.io/sybil-solutions/vllm-dsv41-h200@sha256:cdab2b83 pulled anonymously; its vLLM tree equals the image the numbers were developed on except 5 comment lines, pip freeze identical. Lossless check: greedy completions with per-token logprobs on 12 prompts vs two runs of the development image: mean |dlogprob| 0.031, run-to-run floor 0.026-0.029, every divergence at a near-tie. Sweep run with --vocab-hi 128000 (vocab 129,280; the default 150000 draws ids the server rejects). Prefill uses random tokens, so every Engram lookup misses the GPU row cache and reads from SSD (a hardware RAID volume here): 3.3-4.2k tok/s, vs 29-33k on a real-text corpus. Decode answers are prose with thinking off: DSpark acceptance 2.2-2.6 tokens/step; on code-summary prompts acceptance is 4.3 and 1-user decode is 485-489 tok/s (see target). At C128/C256 the sweep's per-stream budget (context / C) ends some answers by length. needs_measured.gpu_used_peak_mib is replaced by the four used cards: memwatch sums all eight GPUs on the host. Lab acceptance (local-ai-registry lab.py try --on endpoint): load, chat, reasoning, tools, context (175,457 tokens), speed all pass.
